summary:
R4 is the model to lean on today — its strong-play window is scorching at 14d 22-9 (+19.0u) and 30d 62-35 (+38.0u), both the best net units of any rating, and its hitting category is the hottest cell on the board at +11.1pts over baseline (62% last 14, n=72) riding a 5-game win streak. All four ratings are locked in across trends (64%, n=72, 3W streak), runs (60-61%, 4W streaks everywhere) and sp (60-61%), so when today's slate shows trends+sp or trends+runs agreement, that's the sharpest combo available — trends+sp hits 57.9% on the season (n=620) and is the top-ranked pairing. The one category to fade across every rating is bullpen_fatigue, cold at -6.1pts (29-43, 40%) for R1/R2/R3 — any pick where that's the lone supporting category needs a discount, while R4's bullpen_fatigue sits unflagged but still underwater at 45% season-long, so don't let it carry a play alone.

On the board today, prioritize games involving LAD and TBR if they appear — LAD is money when picked, 71% straight (36-15) and elite in strong-play spots at 82% (27-6, +27.0u), while TBR's strong mark is 72% (26-10, +22.0u) with a 69% overall hit rate. BOS is right behind at 70% (39-17) and 76% in strong plays (+19.0u) — any slate intersection where R4's hot hitting cell or a trends+sp agreement lands on LAD, TBR, or BOS is the highest-confidence stack available today. Conversely, treat NYY as a fade target even if the model likes them: 51% overall and a money-losing 39% in strong plays (-4.0u) says the rating's read on that roster isn't translating. With R1-R3 showing matching 14d strong-play profiles (67-69% hit, +14.0u each), today's edge comes less from picking which rating to trust and more from stacking R4's hot hitting signal against the LAD/TBR/BOS trio whenever it appears on the card.
